title: pvCSVReader
body:
## pvCSVReader

Reads delimited text (.csv, .tsv, .txt) into a table (vtkTable): one column per field, typed as numbers when DetectNumericColumns is on (ParaView default), with the first line as column names by default. The ParaView XML calls the output a 1-D rectilinear grid, but the underlying vtkDelimitedTextReader produces a table. Use pvTableToPoints or pvTableToStructuredGrid to turn coordinate columns into geometry; several files form a time series.

Common mistakes and assumptions:

- The default delimiter is a comma only; set FieldDelimiterCharacters (or AddTabFieldDelimiter for tab-separated files) to match the file.
- A table is not a dataset; filters that need points or cells reject it until it is converted.
- Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this reader, so inspect the output blocks, arrays and time steps on your own files before relying on it.

Native constructor: `CSVReader`. Identity: `sources/CSVReader`. Role: `pipeline`. Output kinds: `["data"]`.

### Inputs

No connected inputs (source/resource).


### Options

| Key | Meaning / native assignment | Type and constraints | Default / required | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `AddTabFieldDelimiter` | This property indicates whether to add the tab character as a field delimiter to the list of other delimiter characters. This is needed since in the GUI the user can't enter a tab character. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `false` |
| `DetectNumericColumns` | When set to true, the reader will detect numeric columns and create vtkDoubleArray or vtkIntArray for those instead of vtkStringArray. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `false` |
| `FieldDelimiterCharacters` | This property lists the characters that may be used to separate fields. For example, a value of "," indicates a comma-separated value file. A value of ".:;" indicates that columns may be separated by a period, colon or semicolon. The order of the characters in the text string does not matter. | `{"type":"string"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `"REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"` |
| `FileName` | The list of files to be read by the reader. Each file is expected to be a csv file. If more than one file is specified, the reader will switch to file series mode in which it will pretend that it can support time and provide one file per time step. Fixed at construction; cannot vary per visit. | `{"items":{"minLength":1,"type":"string"},"minItems":1,"type":"array"}` | `required` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |
| `HaveHeaders` | If the value of this property is 1, treat the first line of the file as headers. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `false` |
| `MergeConsecutiveDelimiters` | Whether to merge successive delimiters. Use this if (for example) your fields are separated by spaces but you don't know exactly how many. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `false` |
| `UseStringDelimiter` | This property indicates whether to use the string delimiter. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `false` |

Execution contract:

```json
{
  "mode": "serial",
  "performance": "unknown"
}
```

Coverage and unbound native properties:

```json
{
  "defaults": "native defaults for omitted options",
  "gaps": {},
  "origin": "generated",
  "output": "native inspection required; explicit output-port selection available",
  "outputPorts": null,
  "qualification": "not-run"
}
```

### Syntax example

Place in `nodes`. Data outputs may be selected by a scene; resource outputs must be connected to a compatible consumer.

```json
{
  "id": "result",
  "filter": "pvCSVReader",
  "options": {
    "FileName": [
      "REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"
    ]
  }
}
```
